blocks.explanation:
Write \(\frac{1}{\sin^2 x} = \csc^2 x\); then it is algebraic times trigonometric.
Plan: \(x\) first, \(\csc^2 x\) second (its integral is \(-\cot x\)), then \(\int \cot x\,dx = \ln|\sin x|\).
steps:
Given: \(\int \frac{x}{\sin^2 x}\,dx\).
To find: the indefinite integral.
Method: rewrite as \(\int x\csc^2 x\,dx\); integration by parts with \(f(x) = x\), \(g(x) = \csc^2 x\).

Rewrite
\[\int \dfrac{x}{\sin^2 x}\,dx = \int x\csc^2 x\,dx\]
Why: \(\csc x = \frac{1}{\sin x}\).

Apply integration by parts
\[= x(-\cot x) - \int (-\cot x)\cdot 1\,dx\]
\[= -x\cot x + \int \dfrac{\cos x}{\sin x}\,dx\]
Why: \(\frac{d}{dx}\cot x = -\csc^2 x\), so \(\int \csc^2 x\,dx = -\cot x\).

Numerator is the derivative of the denominator
\[= -x\cot x + \ln|\sin x| + c\]
Why: \(\frac{d}{dx}\sin x = \cos x\) and \(\int \frac{f'(x)}{f(x)}\,dx = \ln|f(x)| + c\).

Check
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}(-x\cot x + \ln|\sin x|)\]
\[= -\cot x + x\csc^2 x + \cot x\]
\[= x\csc^2 x\]
Why: product rule; the \(\cot x\) terms cancel.
